title: Guitar basics & how to hold it
summary: Parts of the guitar, sitting/standing posture, hand positioning.
content: Your guitar has a body, neck, headstock, and 6 strings running over frets. Sit with the guitar's curve resting on your right leg (if right-handed), neck angled slightly up, your fretting hand thumb behind the neck (not wrapped over the top), and your strumming hand relaxed over the sound hole/pickups.

title: String names & fretboard layout
summary: E A D G B E, and how frets raise pitch.
content: From thickest to thinnest: E-A-D-G-B-E (mnemonic: 'Eddie Ate Dynamite, Good Bye Eddie'). Each fret raises a string's pitch by one half-step. Pressing a string behind a fret and picking it sounds that note.

title: Reading chord diagrams
summary: Vertical lines = strings, horizontal = frets, dots = finger placement.
content: A chord diagram is the fretboard viewed head-on: the 6 vertical lines are strings (thick E on the left), horizontal lines are frets, dots show where to press and with which finger, an 'X' above a string means don't play it, an 'O' means play it open.

title: Tuning your guitar
summary: Using the app tuner to get in standard tuning.
content: Use the Tuner tool. Pluck one string at a time and adjust the tuning peg until the indicator centers. Always tune up into pitch (slightly flat, then raise) for more stable tuning.

title: Basic music theory: notes, beats, measures
summary: What a beat is, what a measure is, what BPM means.
content: Music is organized in beats grouped into measures (bars). BPM (beats per minute) is the tempo — 60 BPM means one beat per second. A time signature like 4/4 means 4 beats per measure.

title: Your first open chords: Em, Am, G, C, D
summary: The five chords behind hundreds of songs.
content: Learn each shape slowly, string by string, checking every note rings clearly before moving on. Use the Chord Library for diagrams and common-mistake tips.

title: Chord transitions
summary: Moving between two chords smoothly and on time.
content: Practice one pair at a time (e.g. Em to Am) slowly with a metronome, moving fingers as a shape rather than one at a time. Speed comes from repetition, not rushing.

title: Strumming patterns & downstrokes/upstrokes
summary: Building a steady down-up strumming hand.
content: Keep your strumming arm moving continuously down-up-down-up even on beats you don't hit strings — that constant motion is what keeps rhythm steady.

title: Rhythm & timing
summary: Counting beats out loud, playing with a metronome.
content: Count '1 & 2 & 3 & 4 &' out loud while strumming. Down strokes usually land on the numbers, up strokes on the 'and's.

title: Intro to scales
summary: The major scale and minor pentatonic shapes.
content: A scale is a set of notes that sound good together in a key. The minor pentatonic is the most common beginner lead-guitar scale — five notes, movable shape.

title: Barre chords
summary: Using one finger to press multiple strings, unlocking any key.
content: Barre chords take hand strength — practice in short daily bursts rather than long sessions. Start with F using only the top 4 strings if the full barre buzzes.

title: Guitar techniques: hammer-ons, pull-offs, slides, palm muting
content: These techniques connect notes smoothly or change their tone. Track each in My Techniques as you practice it.

title: Song practice & progressive exercises
summary: Applying everything to real songs, starting slow.
content: Head to Songs — the recommendation engine will show songs that match what you've actually learned. Always start a new song well below its original tempo.
